libraries.description: Fictional acoustic surveys reuse a recorder across sites; a handover supports both undertakings without making detections interchangeable.

libraries.description: Fictional community broadcasts share a licensed segment but retain distinct programme deliverables and changing running orders.

The daily ferry bulletin is a separate commission; sharing a studio or a presenter does not make it this special.

gold.rationale: The oral-history special has an explicit separate commissioned output.

events.text: Morning ferry bulletin is a weekday service-information programme with its own editor and daily delivery slot. This week's edition may carry a short archive voice clip, but its purpose and sign-off are separate from the Harbour voices special. Keep daily bulletin scripts in their own record.

libraries.description: One fictional banner participates in a restoration and a later exhibition loan; object identity alone cannot collapse those undertakings.

Deliver a condition record and treatment-history folder before the banner returns to its owner. An autumn museum loan is being discussed separately; transport and display arrangements are not part of this commission.

evidence.quote: condition before restoration

evidence.quote: Restoration folder handover for JB-6 is planned for 22 May.

libraries.description: Fictional food-bank routes share a transferred pallet; a supplier-number collision does not identify which route received another delivery.

events.text: West ward pantry delivery is the depot's Thursday route to three neighbourhood pantries, recorded as WW-3. Keep its packing list and delivery receipts together. The school holiday hamper round is another job with different receiving volunteers, even when both leave the same loading bay.

gold.rationale: Named route and receiving network define the pantry undertaking.

evidence.quote: recorded as WW-3

events.text: School holiday hamper round HH-5 will pack family boxes for collection at the youth hall. Its coordinator approves the final box count. This is not an extension of the West ward pantry route; boxes can move between stocks only when the transfer is recorded.

gold.rationale: A distinct distribution objective and coordinator define the hamper project.

evidence.quote: This is not an extension of the West ward pantry route

events.text: WW-3 packing sheet lists twenty-four pantry cartons on the blue trolley. The volunteer has marked the east pantry receipt as still missing. A reused supplier stamp says invoice 118; that stamp alone is not the pantry route identifier because the supplier restarts invoice numbering each month.

gold.rationale: Clear route code and pantry task anchor the source despite a nonunique invoice number.

evidence.quote: WW-3 packing sheet lists twenty-four pantry cartons

events.text: Invoice 118: four cases received, signature unreadable. The saved crop omits the month, route and receiving venue, and neither volunteer recognises the handwriting. Repeated supplier numbering means this fragment cannot show whether the cases went to WW-3 or HH-5.

gold.rationale: A duplicate number without month or receiver is insufficient for assignment.

evidence.quote: omits the month, route and receiving venue

events.text: Transfer slip T9 removes one unopened cereal pallet from WW-3 pantry stock and adds it to HH-5 hamper stock. Both coordinators signed the adjustment. This one slip must be available with both delivery records so neither counts the transferred stock twice.

gold.rationale: A single stock transfer changes both operational projects without making their routes identical.

evidence.quote: removes one unopened cereal pallet from WW-3 pantry stock and adds it to HH-5 hamper stock

events.text: HH-5 collection note: the youth hall doors open at 13:00 for hamper collection. Volunteers arrive half an hour earlier to lay out the boxes. The note is about this holiday round only; it gives no opening time for the West ward pantries.

gold.rationale: The specific collection event continues HH-5.

evidence.quote: the youth hall doors open at 13:00

events.reason: The depot duplicate has the WW-3 route stamp. File the cropped invoice with West ward pantry delivery only.

gold.rationale: Explicit user comparison to the duplicate resolves the ambiguous fragment.

events.text: Depot template explains the difference between received, transferred and delivered columns. It is saved as background for both route coordinators. libraries.description: Fictional coastal mapping commissions share coordinates and a boat trip but distinguish accessibility mapping from shoreline-change survey outputs.

events.text: Pebble bay accessible-path map will document benches, entrances and step-free route descriptions for the visitor centre. Use visitor map sheet V2 for annotations. The coast science group's shoreline atlas has a different deliverable, even where the two maps cover exactly the same beach.

gold.rationale: Accessibility information for the visitor centre defines a distinct mapping purpose.

events.text: Pebble bay shoreline-change atlas compares surveyed shoreline traces for the coast science group. Use survey sheet S8 and keep its reference-frame label attached to every coordinate extract. This atlas does not certify accessible paths or replace the visitor centre's V2 map.

gold.rationale: Shoreline comparison is a separate deliverable despite geographic overlap.

evidence.quote: Use survey sheet S8

events.text: Boat booking PB-11 takes the V2 visitor-map photographer and the S8 shoreline survey recorder to the north landing on the same trip. Each team has its own capture list. The shared booking connects logistics, not the meanings or reference frames of their measurements.

evidence.quote: the V2 visitor-map photographer and the S8 shoreline survey recorder

events.text: North landing coordinate extract, point 14. The cropped image contains two numbers but neither a map-sheet code nor a reference-frame label. Both teams visited this landing. The coordinate values alone cannot identify which mapping deliverable this particular extract supports.

events.text: V2 north landing walk-through: photograph the bench beside the visitor sign and record the entrance wording exactly. The speaker calls the beach pebble bank once, but the V2 sheet is visible. No shoreline trace measurements are requested in this visitor-map clip.
